rows.subtype: Approach: scoring options against agreed criteria [Action]
rows.description: The group first agrees on criteria such as customer impact, cost and risk, then scores the options together, making the discussion about facts instead of personalities.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, constraint-based thinking, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: avoiding the decision through more meetings [Pitfall]
rows.description: The lead keeps asking for further input to avoid upsetting anyone. Weeks pass, the deadline is missed, and every group ends up unhappy with the delay.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: constraint-based thinking, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: one-on-one conversations before the group meeting [Action]
rows.description: The lead talks privately with each stakeholder to understand fears and constraints, finding that two conflicts are misunderstandings that vanish before the full meeting begins.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: making a reversible decision and testing [Thinking]
rows.description: Because no one can prove which option is right, the lead chooses one that can be undone cheaply, sets a review date and shares the metrics that would trigger a change.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, constraint-based thinking, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: explaining the decision to those who lost [Revision]
rows.description: After the choice, the lead meets the disappointed team, explains the reasons, and agrees on a follow-up for their concerns, keeping the relationship intact for later decisions.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, constraint-based thinking, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: escalating to a sponsor when deadlocked [Revision]
rows.description: When two directors cannot agree despite talks, the lead brings a neutral summary to the executive sponsor and asks for a ruling, treating escalation as a tool and not as failure.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, constraint-based thinking, negotiation

rows.description: During a payments outage, the on-call engineer chooses to roll back the latest release at once instead of hunting the bug, because customers are failing to pay every minute.

rows.description: The team names one incident commander, one person to investigate, and one to update customers and management, so that people do not duplicate work or shout over each other.

rows.subtype: Approach: everyone trying random fixes at once [Pitfall]
rows.description: Five engineers change settings simultaneously without telling one another. The system state becomes unclear, and it is impossible to know which change helped or hurt.

rows.description: The engineer follows a written checklist: check dashboards, recent deployments, database health and dependencies, in order, which speeds diagnosis when the mind is stressed at three in the morning.
